summary: Generated tonic/prost requests now bridge into existing backbone write-plan adapter boundaries without opening sockets.
claim_boundary: Generated request-to-write-plan adapter seam only. This slice converts source-controlled tonic/prost generated messages for messenger, mail, social, and community write RPCs into the existing framework-free API/app write-plan entrypoints. It does not implement a tonic server, live gRPC client, listener, gateway, broker publisher, database executor, deployment pipeline run, SLO, or delivery guarantee.

source_basis.use: Official Proto3 language specification used for the source-controlled request/response/enum/oneof contract shape consumed by the generated adapter.
Official tonic-build documentation used for the generated module/include_proto pattern established in the prior generated-adapter slice.
Official tonic documentation for the current generated service/message ecosystem and the boundary between generated bindings and transport runtime features.

facets.F1_simplicity: A single generated adapter crate owns generated-message conversion into already-existing gRPC write-plan functions; domain/API/usecase/app crates remain free of tonic/prost transport coupling.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The seam makes the proto-generated edge testable before runtime listeners exist, preserving a small contract surface that can later be wrapped by independently scalable server/client adapters.
facets.F3_adversarial: Focused tests prove valid generated messenger/mail/social/community requests reach write-plan boundaries and invalid enum or missing oneof/context messages are rejected before app execution.
facets.F4_api_contract: Generated enum and oneof fields are mapped into typed API request/envelope enums for messenger, mail/DMARC, social artifact kinds, community modes, vote directions, and moderation verbs.
facets.F5_quality: Focused generated-adapter tests plus the 44-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F6_operations: No operational service is started; the adapter is deliberately limited to deterministic in-process write-plan construction so future tonic transport can be added as a separate auditable slice.
facets.F7_security_privacy: Conversion preserves tenant/principal/idempotency/policy/audit reference fields and encrypted-envelope references only; no raw content, credentials, broker URLs, database URLs, or secret material are introduced.
facets.F8_supply_chain: No new third-party dependency is added in this slice; the generated adapter gains only internal workspace crate dependencies needed to call existing write-plan boundaries.
facets.F9_testing: Focused tests passed for 9 generated-adapter unit tests and the broad backbone matrix passed 283 unit tests plus the existing ignored metrics adapter doctest.
facets.F10_ci_cd: Static CI/Jenkins matrices already include the generated adapter from the prior slice; this slice adds local evidence only and does not claim remote CI execution.
facets.F11_observability: Adapter responses continue to expose the fully qualified gRPC method metadata and receipt policy/audit/idempotency references that future interceptors and traces must bind to.
facets.F13_reversibility: The generated request conversion layer is isolated to one adapter crate plus catalog/task/evidence metadata; reverting it removes the bridge without changing business logic crates.
